label: catalogue-shortform-60
what_this_is: 60 real short-form Arabic item lines read from construction.items in the live farq-main project (read-only SELECT). Real supplier-catalogue product names in the register the owner uploads: two to five words, no supply verb, no specification tail.
what_this_is_not: This is NOT the owner's real 60-line RFQ. That RFQ lives in the `farq` Supabase project, which is INACTIVE/paused; unpausing production infrastructure is outside a read-only analysis, so it was not touched. The active `farq-main` project holds 2 rfq_lines in total. This sample is the closest real substitute available and is named as a substitute everywhere it is reported.
adjudication_authority: Adjudicated by the cascade lane, NOT by the owner. Weaker than the 68-item booklet table, which is the owner's register and has been adjudicated across five generations. Where the two disagree in method, the booklet wins.
method: Each line was assigned an expected family and, where one legitimately exists, an expected intent — using the item's own catalogue `category` column and the payload's family list, BEFORE either engine was run on it. `null` family means no trade in this ontology owns the line and the correct behaviour is abstention. `null` intent means the family IS the complete answer and inventing an intent would fragment the supplier pool.
known_bias: The sample is plumbing- and electrical-heavy because that is what a random draw from this catalogue returned. It under-represents civil, finishes and safety, so it measures the fittings/cables register well and says nothing about the rest.
source_query: select name_ar, category from construction.items where name_ar ~ '^[\u0600-\u06FF\s]+$' and char_length(name_ar) between 8 and 45 and category in (...) order by md5(id::text||'s2') limit 80
